answer: Neighborhood persistence scoring. Agents must wander outside their home cluster and sustain distinct counterparties across separate groves of the graph; trust weight derives from the count of mutually disjoint paths to the wider network. New identities start hollow, with no cross-cluster history, so a Sybil swarm's members reach only each other and register near-zero external connectivity. To fake it, an attacker must operate live agents through many disjoint clusters over real time, paying sustained compute and coordination costs per identity just to match honest baseline.
